references.text: God promises to bless the bread and water and remove sickness from the people, a parallel to the promise of blessing in Deuteronomy 7:13.
The promise that God will turn toward the people, make them fruitful and numerous, and confirm His covenant with them.
The same blessings are mentioned: the fruit of the womb, the produce of the ground, the herds and flocks, as part of the covenant blessings.
God promises abundance of goods: the fruit of the womb, the increase of the herds, and the produce of the ground, in the land He swore to give the fathers.
God will give abundance in all work, in the fruit of the womb, the increase of the herds, and the produce of the ground, and rejoice over the people.
The promise to Abraham of blessing and numerous offspring, which is the foundation for the promise given to the fathers.
God repeats the promise to Isaac to give the land to his offspring and bless him, mentioned as an oath to the fathers.
The children of Israel were fruitful and multiplied greatly, a fulfillment of the promise to make the people numerous.
God blesses His people so that they become very numerous, and does not let their herds decrease.
The blessing on the godly includes a fertile wife and children, a parallel to the promise of the fruit of the womb.
A promise that storehouses and vessels will be filled with abundance when one honors the Lord with one's wealth.
A promise of rain in its season and produce from the ground: grain, wine, and oil, as well as grass for the herds.
